intro.title: LRU Cache
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a Least Recently Used (LRU) Cache, a data structure that stores a limited number of items and automatically removes the least recently used one when full. You'll learn how to implement it using a combination of a Map for fast lookups and a Doubly Linked List to track usage order. The core programming concepts involve managing data structures, handling cache eviction logic, and ensuring operations run in constant time. By the end, you'll have a working LRU Cache in JavaScript that can efficiently store and retrieve key-value pairs.
intro.usecase: LRU Cache is essential for optimizing performance in real-world applications where you need to manage limited resources efficiently. You'll find it in web browsers that cache recently visited pages to enable faster back/forward navigation, in database systems that keep frequently accessed records in memory, and in e-commerce sites that store recently viewed products for quick retrieval. As a developer, implementing LRU Cache helps you build responsive dashboards that load user preferences quickly, improve search filter performance by caching recent queries, and create efficient data panels that handle large datasets without slowing down the interface.
